source.title: Measurer’s Handbook: US Army and Marine Corps Anthropometric Surveys, 2010-2011
source.note: 24 direct ANSUR-II targets. v0.8.19.8 preserves reviewed calibration biases while correcting flagged canonical geometry: strict upper-arm isolation, buttock lateral level, separate trapezius proxy, smoother surface paths, linked-landmark line editing and auditable circumference-plane tilt. PROT remains the audit layer over shared MEAS geometry.

standing.label: Anthropometric Standing
standing.description: Erect, weight even, heels together as much as possible, legs/trunk straight without stiffness, head erect, arms relaxed at sides, palms beside thighs.
standing.implementationNote: Native world-direction constraints are applied through the exact SOMA/Axis16→Anny retarget path. Feet target ~2 cm joint separation; no FBX pose or guessed local Euler axis is used.

sitting.label: Anthropometric Sitting
sitting.description: Erect sitting, thighs parallel, knees 90°, feet in line with thighs, shoulders relaxed; upper arms hang at sides; before measuring elbows flex 90°, hands straight, palms inward.
sitting.implementationNote: Native world-direction constraints set thighs horizontal, shins vertical and the ANSUR sitting arm-chain geometry. The whole posed body is translated to the rest-floor level so the feet do not float. Seat-edge gap, physical contact and exact Frankfurt alignment remain visual protocol checks.

chest_breadth_prep.label: Chest Breadth · Setup
chest_breadth_prep.description: Standing, heels together. Both hands on hips while the caliper is aligned. Participant takes and holds a deep breath.
chest_breadth_prep.implementationNote: Hands-on-hips ist eine IK-Näherung. Die volle Inspiration ist eine Protokollbedingung und verändert in dieser Version das Brustvolumen nicht automatisch.

chest_breadth_measure.label: Chest Breadth · Measurement
chest_breadth_measure.description: After full inspiration and caliper alignment, arms are lowered and breadth is measured. Full inspiration is a protocol condition; Sammy V1 pose does not simulate breathing volume.
chest_breadth_measure.implementationNote: Arme werden nach dem Setup abgesenkt. Der Atemzustand bleibt eine nicht volumetrisch simulierte Protokollbedingung.

hip_arms_away.label: Hip Breadth · arms slightly away
hip_arms_away.description: Anthropometric standing with arms held slightly away from the body.
hip_arms_away.implementationNote: „Slightly away“ ist im Handbook nicht als Winkel festgelegt; der Sammy-Winkel ist deshalb ein reproduzierbarer Startwert und muss visuell freigegeben werden.

waist_hand_chest.label: Waist Depth · right hand on chest
waist_hand_chest.description: Anthropometric standing, but with the right hand on the chest.
waist_hand_chest.implementationNote: Hand-auf-Brust ist als reproduzierbarer Rig-Startwert angenähert; entscheidend ist, dass der rechte Arm die Taillenmessung nicht stört.

thigh_special.label: Thigh Circumference · special
thigh_special.description: Standing erect, legs just far enough apart that thighs do not touch; right hand on chest.
thigh_special.implementationNote: Die Beinspreizung ist ein Startwinkel, kein fester ANSUR-Winkel. Pro randomisiertem Körper prüfen, dass sich die Oberschenkel gerade nicht berühren.

lowerleg_10cm.label: Calf / Ankle · ~10 cm stance
lowerleg_10cm.description: Standing erect on table, feet/heels approximately 10 cm apart, weight equally distributed.
lowerleg_10cm.implementationNote: Die 10-cm-Vorgabe ist eine reale Distanz; der weltbasierte Beinrichtung erzeugt je nach Beinlänge nur eine Näherung. Abstand am Mannequin visuell prüfen.

wrist_90.label: Wrist · elbow 90°, palm up
wrist_90.description: Standing, upper arm relaxed, elbow flexed 90°, palm up.
wrist_90.implementationNote: Upper arm relaxed and elbow ≈90° are now native world-direction constraints. Exact forearm supination/palm-up twist remains a visual protocol caveat.

arm_relaxed_palm_forward.label: Arm Length · relaxed / palm forward
arm_relaxed_palm_forward.description: Standing with arms relaxed at sides; for Radiale-Stylion Length the right palm faces forward.
arm_relaxed_palm_forward.implementationNote: Palm-forward ist eine Constraint-Preset-Orientierung und muss visuell geprüft werden; die Arme bleiben ansonsten entspannt an der Seite.

crotch_setup.label: Crotch Height · blade setup
conditions: setup only; return heels together for measurement
crotch_setup.description: Participant first spreads the legs only enough to place the anthropometer blade near the crotch. The heels are then brought back together before the actual height is read.
crotch_setup.implementationNote: Nur Setup-Schritt zum Einführen der Anthropometer-Klinge. Für die eigentliche Messung werden die Fersen wieder zusammengeführt (zweiter Pose-Schritt).

arm_flexed_forward.label: Flexed arm circumference pose
arm_flexed_forward.description: Standing; right upper arm extended forward horizontally, elbow flexed 90°, fist tightly clenched.
arm_flexed_forward.implementationNote: Right upper arm forward/horizontal and elbow ≈90° are now native world-direction constraints. Fist clench and max-effort muscle bulging remain non-deforming protocol conditions.

acromion.label: Acromion
acromion.DESCRIPTION: The point of intersection of the lateral border of the acromial process and a line running down the middle of the shoulder from the neck to the tip of the shoulder.
acromion.PROCEDURE: Participant is in the anthropometric standing position. Stand behind the participant and palpate the tips of both shoulders simultaneously. Draw a line along the lateral bony border of each shoulder. Then stand at the right of the participant, and lay a tape on the shoulder originating at the trapezius point (at the base of the neck), passing so that the front edge of the tape lies over the clavicle (collar bone) point, and crosses the drawn acromial border at the tip of the shoulder. Draw a short line along the front edge of the tape where it crosses the acromial border. Repeat the process for the left shoulder.
acromion.heading: 5.2.1 Acromion, Right and Left

buttock_lateral.label: Buttock Point · lateral
buttock_lateral.DESCRIPTION: Points at the level of the maximum protrusion of the right buttock.
buttock_lateral.PROCEDURE: Participant is in the anthropometric standing position. Stand at the right of the participant and sight the point of maximum protrusion of the right buttock (buttock point, posterior). (This landmark is not drawn.) Set the landmark transfer rod to the height of the posterior buttock landmark. Move it to the right and left sides of the participant and draw short horizontal marks on each side.
buttock_lateral.heading: 5.2.4 Buttock Point, Right Lateral and Left Lateral

cervicale.label: Cervicale · C7
cervicale.DESCRIPTION: The most prominent palpable point of the spine of the seventh cervical vertebra1.
cervicale.PROCEDURE: Participant is in the anthropometric standing position with the head in the Frankfurt plane. The spine of the seventh cervical vertebra is the most prominent vertebral spine of the back of the neck. It is best found by having the participant bend the head downwards. Stand behind the participant and with the pad of the index finger, palpate the most prominent spine. Have the participant slowly bring the head up to the Frankfurt plane while intermittently touching the spine. When the head is in place, locate the most prominent point of the spine of the seventh cervical vertebra. Draw a cross (+) through the landmark.
cervicale.CAUTION: A few participants will be encountered on whom no cervical spine prominence is detectable. On such participants, estimate the point as nearly as possible with respect to the neck and shoulders. A few participants will exhibit two or three equally prominent spinal processes. In such cases, mark the spine that is closest to the posterior base of the neck as established by a tape. Be sure that the head is in the Frankfurt plane when the landmark is drawn. 1 The definition used in ANSUR refers to the “superior palpable point” rather than to the most prominent point. This change was made to bring the definition into compliance with standard anatomical usage (Martin, 1914) and international practice.
cervicale.heading: 5.2.5 Cervicale

chest_point.label: Chest Point · anterior
chest_point.DESCRIPTION: The most anterior right point on the chest.
chest_point.PROCEDURE: Participant is in the anthropometric standing position. Stand at the right of the participant and sight the most protruding right point of the chest. For women place an adhesive dot on the bra and for men draw a cross (+) on the chest. Draw a cross on the adhesive dot prior to placing it on the bra.
chest_point.CAUTION: After placing the mark move to the front of the participant and verify that the landmark is properly placed. 2 This landmark is unchanged from ANSUR for female participants. For male participants, the ANSUR Thelion landmark, at the center of the nipple (unmarked) was used. Dimensions taken at that landmark often missed the largest portion of the chest, which is needed for determining clearance as well as clothing and protection. Now, the anterior point is used for both males and females.
chest_point.heading: 5.2.6 Chest point, anterior, right2

gluteal_furrow.label: Gluteal Furrow Point
gluteal_furrow.DESCRIPTION: The lowest point of the lowest furrow or crease at the juncture of the right buttock and the thigh.
gluteal_furrow.PROCEDURE: Participant is in the anthropometric standing position. Stand behind the participant and draw a short horizontal line at the top of the thigh at the lowest point of the lowest crease. Where there is a smooth continuous curve at the juncture of the thigh and buttock, view the buttock/thigh juncture from the right side and draw the landmark where you judge it to be appropriate. Even on participants with a continuous curve, a skin crease can usually be discerned.
gluteal_furrow.heading: 5.2.15 Gluteal Furrow Point

infrathyroid.label: Infrathyroid
infrathyroid.DESCRIPTION: The inferior point of the thyroid cartilage (Adam's apple) in the midsagittal plane.
infrathyroid.PROCEDURE: Participant stands with the head in the Frankfurt plane. Stand in front of the participant and palpate the smooth lateral surface of the thyroid cartilage moving downwards until you feel the space between the thyroid cartilage and the cricoid cartilage just below it. Then locate the bottom point of the thyroid cartilage in the midsagittal plane. Draw a short horizontal line through the landmark.
infrathyroid.CAUTION: Be sure the participant's head is in the Frankfurt plane.
infrathyroid.heading: 5.2.18 Infrathyroid

neck_base_points.label: Neck Base · anterior/lateral
neck_base_points.DESCRIPTION: Anterior and lateral points at the base of the neck.
neck_base_points.PROCEDURE: Participant stands looking straight ahead. Stand behind the participant. Place a tape around the base of the neck, laying it first in front, then on the sides, and finally, across the back, as if to measure NECK CIRCUMFERENCE, BASE. The anterior landmark is at the bottom of the tape, on the front of the neck in the midsagittal plane. The participant places a finger on the tape near the anterior landmark to help hold the tape in place. Draw a short horizontal line through the landmark. The right lateral and left lateral landmarks are located at the bottom of the tape on both sides. Draw roughly 4 cm long horizontal lines through both landmarks following the bottom of the tape.
neck_base_points.heading: 5.2.29 Neck, Anterior, Right Lateral, and Left Lateral

radiale.label: Radiale
radiale.DESCRIPTION: The superior point on the outside edge of the radius.
radiale.PROCEDURE: Participant stands relaxed. Stand at the right of the participant and palpate the area of the landmark (the hollow on the lateral side of the elbow). When you have located the upper end of the radius, bring the forefinger toward it horizontally, and touch it gently so as not to pull the skin around it up or down. Draw a cross (+) through the point. If you have any difficulty locating this point, grasp the participant's wrist, and rotate the arm back and forth while palpating the bone in the area of the landmark.
radiale.heading: 5.2.33 Radiale

stylion.label: Stylion
stylion.DESCRIPTION: The inferior point of the bottom of the radius and the extension of this landmark on the dorsal and ventral sides of the wrist.
stylion.PROCEDURE: Participant stands with right elbow flexed 90°. Stand in front of the participant and grasp the participant's hand. Place your thumb on the thumb side of the participant's hand and palpate up toward the wrist until you locate the end of the radius. Draw a cross (+) over the landmark. Hold the participant’s hand with the palm facing medially and look directly at the stylion landmark to eliminate errors in sighting. Draw a line across the dorsal (back) surface of the wrist, beginning below stylion. Next draw a line on the ventral (front) surface of the wrist, beginning below stylion.
stylion.CAUTION: This area is crossed by tendons so it may be necessary to bend the hand up and down at the wrist to find the landmark. When transferring, be sure the lines are straight and that their origin is at stylion.
stylion.heading: 5.2.36 Stylion, Dorsal Stylion, and Ventral Stylion

tibiale.label: Tibiale
tibiale.DESCRIPTION: The superior palpable point on the medial condyle of the right tibia.
tibiale.PROCEDURE: Participant stands erect on a table with the weight distributed equally on both feet. Stand in front of the participant and, with one hand, grasp the bony prominences (condyles) located on the left and right side at the top of the tibia. Have the participant flex the knee to help locate these structures. The participant then straightens the knee. When you have located the superior palpable point on the medial condyle of the tibia, use the thumb or index finger of the other hand to mark its place, and draw a cross (+) through the landmark.
tibiale.CAUTION: This landmark is difficult or impossible to locate accurately in heavily muscled participants. Use your best judgment in these cases.
tibiale.heading: 5.2.41 Tibiale

trapezius.label: Trapezius Point
trapezius.DESCRIPTION: The point at which the anterior border of the trapezius muscle crosses the lateral neck landmark.
trapezius.REQUIRED LANDMARKS: Neck, right lateral and left lateral.
trapezius.PROCEDURE: Participant stands looking straight ahead. Ask the participant to place the right hand on his/her left shoulder to help outline the trapezius muscle on the right shoulder. Stand at the side of the participant. Moving from the shoulder to the neck, palpate the mass of the trapezius muscle to locate its anterior border. Draw a short line from the neck toward the shoulder at the point where the anterior border of the muscle crosses the lateral neck landmark. Repeat this procedure on the other side.
trapezius.heading: 5.2.43 Trapezius Point, Right and Left

trochanterion.label: Trochanterion
trochanterion.DESCRIPTION: The superior point of the greater trochanter of the right femur of a standing participant.
trochanterion.PROCEDURE: Participant stands erect with weight distributed equally on both feet. Stand in front of the participant. Use the pads of the fingers to simultaneously locate both greater trochanters (near the hip joint). Work fingers up along the front and back of the right trochanter to find its highest point. On a number of participants it will help to have the participant move the thigh back and forth. Draw a cross (+) at the level of the landmark. On heavier participants be sure to palpate directly horizontally, and avoid moving flesh either above or below the landmark.
trochanterion.CAUTION: This can be a difficult landmark to locate and you may have to use your best judgment in drawing it.
trochanterion.heading: 5.2.45 Trochanterion

waist_omphalion.label: Waist · Omphalion A/P/L/R
waist_omphalion.DESCRIPTION: Center of the navel and its posterior and lateral extensions.
waist_omphalion.PROCEDURE: Participant is in the anthropometric standing position. Stand in front of the participant and locate the landmark by inspection. Draw a 4-cm horizontal line to the right side of omphalion, and using a landmark transfer rod set at the height of omphalion, draw 4-cm horizontal lines on the right and left sides and over the spine of the participant. The landmarks are drawn at the maximum point of quiet respiration. On heavy participants, the navel may point downward, instead of anteriorly. On such participants, continue to follow the procedures outlined above.
waist_omphalion.CAUTION: The participant must not tense the abdominal muscles or change body position while these marks are drawn.
waist_omphalion.heading: 5.2.46 Waist (Omphalion), Right, Left, Anterior, and Posterior

crotch.label: Crotch · undrawn
crotch.heading: 5.1 Undrawn Landmarks · Crotch
crotch.DESCRIPTION: The point at the level of the lower edge of the pubis bone of the os coxa.

vertex.label: Vertex · top of head
vertex.heading: 5.1 Undrawn Landmarks · Top of head (vertex)
vertex.DESCRIPTION: The highest point on the head when the head is in the Frankfurt plane.

buttock_posterior.label: Buttock Point · posterior
buttock_posterior.heading: 5.1 Undrawn Landmarks · Buttock point, posterior
buttock_posterior.DESCRIPTION: Point of maximum protrusion of the right buttock of a standing participant.

calf_max.label: Calf maximum zone
calf_max.DESCRIPTION: No drawn landmark. ANSUR locates the maximum horizontal circumference by measuring three locations in the observed maximum calf area.
calf_max.heading: Dynamic measurement zone · Calf

ankle_min.label: Ankle minimum zone
ankle_min.DESCRIPTION: No drawn landmark. ANSUR defines the ankle measure as the minimum horizontal circumference of the ankle.
ankle_min.heading: Dynamic measurement zone · Ankle

biceps_point.label: Biceps Point · right
biceps_point.DESCRIPTION: The highest point of the right flexed biceps brachii muscle as viewed from the participant’s right side.
biceps_point.PROCEDURE: Participant stands with the right upper arm extended forward horizontally and the elbow flexed 90°. The fist is tightly clenched and held facing the head. Locate the highest point on the flexed biceps brachii muscle and mark a short line perpendicular to the long axis of the upper arm.
biceps_point.mappingNote: PROT currently places a geometric proxy until the flexed-arm base modifier is validated.

elbow_crease.label: Elbow Crease · right
elbow_crease.DESCRIPTION: The skin crease on the inside of the elbow joint when the elbow is flexed 90°.
elbow_crease.mappingNote: Undrawn ANSUR landmark; PROT uses the right elbow/forearm junction as a review proxy until the flexed-arm modifier is validated.

measures.label: Stature
measures.DESCRIPTION: The vertical distance from a standing surface to the top of the head.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant is in the anthropometric standing position with the head in the Frankfurt plane. Stand at one side of the participant, and use an anthropometer to measure the vertical distance between the standing surface and the top of the head. Move the blade of the anthropometer across the top of the head to ensure measurement of the maximum distance. Use firm pressure to compress the participant's hair. The measurement is taken at the maximum point of quiet respiration.
measures.CAUTION: Be sure that the head is in the Frankfurt plane.
measures.heading: 6.4.76 Stature

measures.label: Biacromial Breadth
measures.DESCRIPTION: The distance between the right and left acromion landmarks on the tips of the shoulder.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant is in the anthropometric sitting position. Stand behind the participant, and use a beam caliper to measure the distance between the drawn right and left acromion landmarks at the tips of the shoulders. The beam should be parallel to the coronal plane. If the acromial landmarks cannot be seen from behind, stand in front of the participant. The measurement is taken at the maximum point of quiet respiration. Use sufficient pressure to maintain firm contact with the skin.
measures.CAUTION: The participant must not be allowed to change the position of the shoulders.
measures.heading: 6.4.9 Biacromial Breadth
measures.implementationNote: Direct Acromion-L/R landmark distance; historical shoulder-joint/span proxy removed.

measures.label: Chest Circumference
measures.DESCRIPTION: The maximum circumference of the chest at the fullest part of the breast7.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant is in the anthropometric standing position in front of a mirror. Stand in front of the participant, and use a tape to measure the horizontal circumference of the chest at the level of the right chest point anterior landmark. On women, the landmark will be an adhesive dot on the bra. Before taking the measurement verify that this landmark has not shifted. Use the mirror to check the position of the tape as it crosses the participant’s back. This dimension will cross very soft tissue at the armpit and bust, and some compression of the tissue will inevitably occur. Be sure, however, to keep this to a minimum. Exert only enough tension on the tape to maintain contact between the tape and the skin. The tape will span body hollows in this measurement. The measurement is taken at the maximum point of quiet respiration.
measures.INSTRUMENT: Steel tape. 7 In ANSUR this measurement was taken (in males) at the level of Thelion (nipple). This change was made in order to capture the circumference of the chest at its maximum. It is unchanged for females.
measures.heading: 6.4.25 Chest Circumference

measures.label: Chest Breadth
measures.DESCRIPTION: The maximum horizontal breadth of the chest at the level of the chest point anterior landmark6.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant stands erect looking straight ahead with the heels together and the weight distributed evenly on both feet. The participant places both hands on the hips. Stand in front of the participant, and ready the beam caliper by lining up the blades at the level of chest point anterior. Ask the participant to take a deep breath and hold it. Compress the tissue firmly to ensure contact with the rib cage, ask the participant to lower the arms, and take the measurement. The measurement is taken at maximum inspiration of the chest at the level of the chest point anterior landmark. On women, the landmark will be an adhesive dot on the bra. Before taking the measurement verify that this landmark has not shifted.
measures.CAUTION: Breast tissue should NOT be included in this measurement. This can be avoided, when necessary, by tilting the blades of the caliper upwards and approaching the bony sides of the chest from below the breasts. Additionally, unlike most other dimensions, which are measured at the maximum point of quiet respiration, this dimension is measured at full inspiration. 6 In ANSUR this measurement was taken (in males) at the level of Thelion (nipple). This change was made in order to capture the breadth of the chest at its maximum. It is unchanged for females.
measures.heading: 6.4.24 Chest Breadth

measures.label: Chest Depth
measures.DESCRIPTION: The horizontal distance between the right chest point anterior landmark and the back at the same level8.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant is in the anthropometric standing position. Stand at the right of the participant, and use a beam caliper to measure the horizontal distance between the chest at the level of the right chest point anterior landmark and the back at the same level. Place the fixed blade of the caliper on the back. On women, the landmark will be an adhesive dot on the bra. Before taking the measurement verify that this landmark has not shifted. This measurement is taken at the maximum point of quiet respiration. Exert only enough pressure to maintain contact between the caliper and the skin (or bra).
measures.CAUTION: Participant must not be allowed to change the position of the shoulders. 8 In ANSUR this measurement was taken (in males) at the level of Thelion (nipple). This change was made in order to capture the depth of the chest at its maximum. It is unchanged for females.
measures.heading: 6.4.26 Chest Depth

measures.label: Waist Circumference (Omphalion)
measures.DESCRIPTION: The horizontal circumference of the waist at the level of omphalion encompassing the waist (omphalion) landmarks.
measures.DRAWN LANDMARKS: Waist (omphalion), right, left, anterior and posterior.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant is in the anthropometric standing position in front of a mirror. Stand in front of the participant, and use a tape to measure the horizontal distance around the torso at the level of the center of the navel. The tape will pass over the drawn waist (omphalion) landmarks at the front, back and sides. Use the mirror to check the position of the tape as it crosses the participant's back. Exert only enough tension on the tape to maintain contact between the tape and the body. The measurement is made at the maximum point of quiet respiration.
measures.CAUTION: The participant must not tense the abdominal muscles.
measures.heading: 6.4.88 Waist Circumference (Omphalion)

measures.label: Waist Breadth
measures.DESCRIPTION: The horizontal breadth of the waist at the level of omphalion.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant is in the anthropometric standing position. Stand in front of the participant, and use a beam caliper to measure the horizontal breadth of the waist from the drawn landmark at right waist (omphalion) to the drawn landmark at left waist (omphalion). Exert only enough pressure to attain contact between the caliper and the skin. The measurement is taken at the maximum point of quiet respiration.
measures.CAUTION: Care must be taken not to compress the soft tissue.
measures.heading: 6.4.87 Waist Breadth

measures.label: Waist Depth
measures.DESCRIPTION: The horizontal distance between the front and the back of the waist at the level of omphalion.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant is in the anthropometric standing position, but with the right hand on the chest. Stand at the right of the participant, and use a beam caliper to measure the horizontal distance between the drawn landmarks at waist (omphalion), posterior and waist (omphalion), anterior. The fixed blade of the caliper is on the back. Exert only enough pressure to attain contact between the caliper and the skin. The measurement is taken at the maximum point of quiet respiration.
measures.CAUTION: The participant must not tense the abdominal muscles.
measures.heading: 6.4.89 Waist Depth

measures.label: Buttock Circumference
measures.DESCRIPTION: The horizontal circumference of the trunk at the level of the maximum protrusion of the right buttock.
measures.DRAWN LANDMARKS: Buttock point, right lateral and left lateral.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant stands erect on a table with heels together. Ask the participant to hold up the right leg of the shorts to expose the landmark. Stand at the participant’s right, and use a tape to measure the horizontal circumference of the trunk at the level of the maximum protrusion of the right buttock. The tape should pass over the posterior buttock point (not drawn) and the buttock point landmarks drawn on the right and left hips. If necessary, ask male participants to adjust the genitalia so as to interfere as little as possible with the tape. Exert only enough tension on the tape to maintain contact between the tape and the skin.
measures.CAUTION: The tape must be maintained in a horizontal plane.
measures.heading: 6.4.17 Buttock Circumference
measures.implementationNote: Horizontal strict pelvis slice at the dynamically found maximum posterior right-buttock level.

measures.label: Hip Breadth
measures.DESCRIPTION: The horizontal distance between the lateral buttock landmarks on the sides of the hips.
measures.DRAWN LANDMARKS: Buttock point, right lateral and left lateral.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant is in the anthropometric standing position with the arms held slightly away from the body. Stand in front of the participant, and use a beam caliper to measure the horizontal distance between the drawn lateral buttock landmarks. If necessary, have the participant hold the sides of the shorts above the landmarks. Exert only enough pressure to ensure that the caliper blades are on the hips.
measures.CAUTION: Make sure participants do not pull soft tissue when they hold up their shorts.
measures.heading: 6.4.51 Hip Breadth
measures.implementationNote: Direct horizontal distance between lateral buttock landmarks at the same level as Buttock Circumference.

measures.label: Crotch Height
measures.DESCRIPTION: The vertical distance between the standing surface and the crotch.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant stands on a table in the anthropometric standing position. Stand in front of the participant. Ask the participant to spread the legs apart enough to allow placement of the blade of an anthropometer near the crotch. The participant then brings the heels back together and raises the blade until it is in firm contact with the crotch. (Place the blade to the right of the genitalia.) The measurer then exerts additional upward pressure on the slide of the anthropometer to achieve firm and uniform placement. Measure the vertical distance between the standing surface and the crotch.
measures.CAUTION: The computer will add 1 cm to the recorded dimension to account for the width of the anthropometer blade.
measures.heading: 6.4.28 Crotch Height

measures.label: Neck Circumference
measures.DESCRIPTION: The circumference of the neck at the level of the infrathyroid landmark (Adam’s apple).
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant is in the anthropometric standing position with the head in the Frankfurt plane. Stand at the right of the participant, and use a tape to measure the circumference of the neck at the level of the drawn infrathyroid landmark. The plane of the measurement is perpendicular to the long axis of the neck. Exert only enough tension on the tape to maintain contact between the tape and the skin.
measures.CAUTION: Be sure that the participant's head is in the Frankfurt plane.
measures.heading: 6.4.63 Neck Circumference
measures.implementationNote: Strict neck slice at the Infrathyroid landmark level, perpendicular to the local neck axis.

measures.label: Neck Circumference, Base
measures.DESCRIPTION: The circumference of the base of the neck encompassing the lateral neck and anterior neck landmarks.
measures.DRAWN LANDMARKS: Neck, anterior, right lateral, and left lateral.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant is in the anthropometric standing position with the head in the Frankfurt plane. Stand behind the participant, and use a tape to measure the circumference of the base of the neck. The tape passes over the drawn lateral and anterior neck landmarks. Exert only enough tension on the tape to maintain contact between the tape and the skin. The participant will hold the tape on the anterior neck landmark.
measures.CAUTION: Be sure that the participant's head is in the Frankfurt plane.
measures.heading: 6.4.64 Neck Circumference, Base

measures.label: Wrist Circumference
measures.DESCRIPTION: The circumference of the wrist at the level of stylion and perpendicular to the long axis of the forearm.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant stands with the upper arm relaxed and the elbow flexed 90° with the palm up. Stand in front of the participant, and use a tape to measure the circumference of the wrist perpendicular to the long axis of the forearm. When correctly placed, the upper edge of the tape will run just below the bony prominence at stylion, and the lower edge of the tape will run just above the pisiform bone at the bottom of the little finger side of the hand. Exert only enough tension on the tape to maintain contact between the tape and the skin.
measures.heading: 6.4.93 Wrist Circumference
measures.implementationNote: Strict right-wrist slice at Stylion level, perpendicular to local forearm axis; not a minimum search.

measures.label: Thigh Circumference
measures.DESCRIPTION: The circumference of the thigh at its juncture with the buttock.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant stands erect on a table with the weight distributed equally on both feet. The legs are spread apart just enough so that the thighs do not touch, and the right hand is on the chest. Stand at the right of the participant, and use a tape to measure the circumference of the thigh at its juncture with the buttock (gluteal furrow point). The measurement is made perpendicular to the long axis of the thigh. Exert only enough tension on the tape to maintain contact between the tape and the skin.
measures.CAUTION: The participant must not tense the thigh muscles. The tape must not be placed in a furrow.
measures.heading: 6.4.79 Thigh Circumference
measures.implementationNote: Strict right-thigh slice at dynamic Gluteal Furrow level, perpendicular to local thigh axis.

measures.label: Calf Circumference
measures.DESCRIPTION: The maximum horizontal circumference of the right calf. PROCEDURE5: Participant stands erect on a table with the heels approximately 10 cm apart, and the weight distributed equally on both feet. Stand at the right of the participant. With a tape held in the horizontal plane measure the circumference of the calf at three locations in the area of observed maximum circumference. Record all three values. Exert only enough tension on the tape to maintain contact between the tape and the skin.
measures.INSTRUMENT: Steel tape. 5 In ANSUR, the level of the circumference was found by sliding the horizontal tape up and down the thigh until the maximum was achieved. The current procedure is faster and produces equivalent results (Hotzman et al., 2010).
measures.heading: 6.4.22 Calf Circumference
measures.implementationNote: Dynamic maximum horizontal circumference search restricted to RIGHT_CALF.

measures.label: Ankle Circumference
measures.DESCRIPTION: Minimum horizontal circumference of the ankle.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant stands on a table with the feet about 10 cm apart and the weight distributed equally on both feet. Stand at the right of the participant and, with a tape, measure the minimum horizontal circumference of the ankle. Exert only enough tape tension to maintain contact between the tape and the skin.
measures.heading: 6.4.5 Ankle Circumference
measures.implementationNote: Dynamic minimum horizontal circumference search restricted to RIGHT_ANKLE.

measures.label: Waist Back Length (Omphalion)
measures.DESCRIPTION: The surface distance between the cervicale landmark at the back of the neck and the waist (omphalion), posterior landmark.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant is in the anthropometric standing position with the head in the Frankfurt plane. Stand behind the participant, and use a tape to measure the vertical surface distance between the landmarks at cervicale and waist (omphalion), posterior. The tape follows body contours. For women the tape passes underneath the bra. Place the zero point of the tape on cervicale. Exert only enough pressure to prevent slack in the tape. The measurement is taken at the maximum point of quiet respiration.
measures.CAUTION: Be sure that the head is in the Frankfurt plane and that the zero point of the tape is on the cervicale landmark when the measurement is made. The measurer will often have to hold the tape against the participant's back to maintain skin contact.
measures.heading: 6.4.86 Waist Back Length (Omphalion)
measures.implementationNote: Surface polyline from Cervicale to posterior Waist (Omphalion), following back contour.

measures.label: Acromion-Radiale Length
measures.DESCRIPTION: The distance between the acromion landmark on the right shoulder and the radiale landmark on the right elbow.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant is in the anthropometric standing position. Stand to the right of the participant, and use a beam caliper to measure the distance between the drawn acromion landmark on the tip of the right shoulder and the drawn radiale landmark on the elbow. It is important that the beam of the caliper be parallel to the long axis of the arm, and that the fixed blade of the caliper remain on the acromion landmark during this measurement. Both blades of the instrument just touch the body.
measures.CAUTION: Care should be taken not to distort the skin.
measures.heading: 6.4.3 Acromion-Radiale Length

measures.label: Radiale-Stylion Length
measures.DESCRIPTION: The distance between the radiale landmark on the right elbow and the stylion landmark on the right wrist.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant stands with the arms relaxed at the sides and the right palm facing forward. Stand at the right of the participant and use a beam caliper to measure the distance between the drawn radiale landmark on the elbow and the drawn stylion landmark on the wrist. Be sure that the beam of the caliper is parallel to the long axis of the arm. Place the fixed blade on radiale. Exert only enough pressure to attain contact between the caliper and the skin.
measures.heading: 6.4.68 Radiale-Stylion Length

measures.label: Biceps Circumference, Flexed
measures.DESCRIPTION: The circumference of the right upper arm at the biceps point landmark.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant stands. The right upper arm is extended forward horizontally and the elbow is flexed about 90°. Place a tape around the upper arm at the level of the drawn biceps point landmark. The fist is clenched and held facing the head. The participant exerts maximum effort in “making a muscle.” The tape is perpendicular to the long axis of the upper arm and only enough tension is used to maintain skin contact.
measures.heading: 6.4.10 Biceps Circumference, Flexed
measures.mappingNote: v0.8.19.8 implements the prescribed arm/elbow geometry and strict measurement region. Max-effort muscle-contraction deformation is not modeled, so this remains a protocol approximation rather than exact soft-tissue equivalence.
measures.implementationNote: Strict RIGHT_UPPER_ARM slice through dynamic Biceps Point in the flexed-arm protocol pose. Actual max-effort muscle deformation is not simulated.

measures.label: Forearm Circumference, Flexed
measures.DESCRIPTION: The circumference at the elbow crease of the flexed right forearm.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant stands with the upper arm extended forward horizontally, the elbow flexed 90°, and the fist tightly clenched. Measure the forearm circumference at the level where the bottom edge of the tape passes across the elbow crease, in a plane perpendicular to the long axis of the forearm. Use only enough tension to maintain skin contact.
measures.CAUTION: Urge the participant to clench the fist tightly.
measures.heading: 6.4.39 Forearm Circumference, Flexed
measures.mappingNote: v0.8.19.8 implements the prescribed arm/elbow geometry and strict measurement region. Max-effort muscle-contraction deformation is not modeled, so this remains a protocol approximation rather than exact soft-tissue equivalence.
measures.implementationNote: Strict RIGHT_FOREARM slice at Elbow Crease in the flexed-arm protocol pose.

measures.label: Tibial Height
measures.DESCRIPTION: The vertical distance between a standing surface and the tibiale landmark.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant stands erect on a table with the feet together and the weight distributed equally on both feet. Stand in front of the participant, and use an anthropometer to measure the vertical distance between the standing surface and the tibiale landmark below the knee on the medial side.
measures.heading: 6.4.82 Tibial Height
measures.implementationNote: Vertical standing-surface height of canonical Tibiale landmark.

measures.label: Shoulder Length
measures.DESCRIPTION: The surface distance between the trapezius landmark and the acromion landmark on the right shoulder.
measures.PROCEDURE: Participant is in the anthropometric standing position. Stand at the right of the participant, and use a tape to measure the surface distance between the drawn trapezius point landmark at the base of the neck and the drawn acromion landmark on the outer border of the shoulder. The zero end of the tape is on the trapezius point.
measures.CAUTION: The participant must not be allowed to change the position of the shoulders.
measures.heading: 6.4.71 Shoulder Length
measures.implementationNote: Surface polyline from right Trapezius to right Acromion.

acromial_height.DESCRIPTION: Vertical distance from the floor to the right acromion landmark.
acromial_height.PROCEDURE: Participant is in the anthropometric standing position. Stand to the right of the participant, and use an anthropometer to measure the vertical distance between the standing surface and the drawn acromion landmark on the tip of the right shoulder. The measurement is made at the maximum point of quiet respiration.
acromial_height.CAUTION: The participant must not be allowed to change the position of the shoulders.
acromial_height.heading: 6.4.2 Acromial Height

trochanterion_height.DESCRIPTION: The vertical distance between a standing surface and the trochanterion landmark on the upper side of the right thigh.
trochanterion_height.PROCEDURE: Participant stands on a table in the anthropometric standing position. Ask the participant to hold up the right leg of the shorts to expose the landmark. Stand at the right of the participant, and use an anthropometer to measure the vertical distance between the standing surface and the drawn trochanterion landmark.
trochanterion_height.heading: 6.4.84 Trochanterion Height

observerErrorGuideline.title: Appendix G · Allowable Observer Error
observerErrorGuideline.description: Allowable interobserver error for dimensions in the 2010-2011 USMC Anthropometric Survey and the U.S. Army Anthropometric Survey. These are protocol reproducibility limits, not population percentiles and not solver target residuals.

protocolRules.defaultRespiration: maximum point of quiet respiration unless the individual dimension states otherwise
protocolRules.frankfurtPlane: When required, the right tragion-right orbitale line is horizontal.
protocolRules.measureScope: Only direct ANSUR II dimensions are included in PROT. Sammy-only derived/internal dimensions are excluded from the protocol review list.
protocolRules.mappingQuality: Direct equivalence and explicit MEAS proxies are distinguished. Proxy measures are included only to expose gaps that must be corrected.

standing.label: ANSUR Standing · native constraints
standing.description: Native SOMA/Axis16 base: pelvis–torso–neck chain upright, straight symmetric legs toward the standing target, arms relaxed at sides. Final visual approval is required.
standing.implementationNote: Native world-direction constraints on the exact SOMA/Axis16 rig. No bundled FBX is retargeted into PROT and no local Euler-axis guess is used.
standing.referenceFileLabel: visual reference only; not loaded or retargeted by PROT

sitting.label: ANSUR Sitting · native constraints
sitting.description: Native SOMA/Axis16 base: pelvis–torso–neck chain upright, thighs horizontal, shins vertical, feet kept in canonical forward/flat orientation, elbows/forearms set from world directions. Whole body is grounded after posing. Final visual approval is required.
sitting.implementationNote: Native world-direction constraints on the exact SOMA/Axis16 rig. Seat-edge distance and support/contact remain visual protocol checks; no FBX retarget is used.
sitting.referenceFileLabel: visual reference only; not loaded or retargeted by PROT

arms_relaxed.label: Arms relaxed at sides
arms_relaxed.description: Returns both arm chains to the reproducible relaxed-side base geometry.

hands_on_hips.label: Hands on hips
hands_on_hips.description: Chest Breadth setup. Retained as an ANSUR instruction but not auto-posed until Standing is visually approved.

arms_slightly_away.label: Arms slightly away
arms_slightly_away.description: ANSUR requires the arms clear for this measurement; automatic angle is intentionally withheld until Standing is approved.

right_hand_on_chest.label: Right hand on chest
right_hand_on_chest.description: Required protocol instruction. Automatic hand-on-chest contact is intentionally withheld until the base poses are approved.

right_elbow_90_palm_up.label: Right elbow 90° · palm up
right_elbow_90_palm_up.description: Wrist posture instruction. Palm twist is not guessed from a local Euler axis.

right_palm_forward.label: Right palm forward
right_palm_forward.description: Lower-arm posture instruction. Palm-forward twist is not guessed from a local Euler axis.

feet_10cm.label: Feet / heels ~10 cm apart
feet_10cm.description: 10 cm stance target solved from native world geometry; weight distribution remains a protocol condition.

thighs_not_touching.label: Thighs just clear
thighs_not_touching.description: Temporary reproducible stance target; final criterion remains visual clearance between the thighs.

crotch_blade_setup.label: Crotch blade setup
crotch_blade_setup.description: Temporary setup only. Actual Crotch Height returns to Standing with heels together.

feet_30cm.label: Feet 30 cm apart
feet_30cm.description: WBX 30 cm stance target. WBX arm/fist detail remains non-production debug.

wbx_arms.label: WBX arms away
wbx_arms.description: WBX debug instruction only; not auto-applied in rescue mode.

rig_debug_a.label: Rig debug A-pose
rig_debug_a.description: Technical symmetry/skinning instruction only; not auto-applied in rescue mode.

sitting_arms_lap.label: Arms on lap
sitting_arms_lap.description: Future seated-protocol instruction; not auto-applied in rescue mode.

sitting_right_hand_chest.label: Sitting · right hand on chest
sitting_right_hand_chest.description: Future seated-protocol instruction; not auto-applied in rescue mode.

right_arm_flexed_forward.label: Right arm forward · elbow 90° · fist clenched
right_arm_flexed_forward.description: Required for ANSUR Biceps Circumference, Flexed and Forearm Circumference, Flexed. Kept as a protocol instruction until this special arm pose is visually validated.

wbx_scan.label: WBX Scan / Region Debug
wbx_scan.description: Optional scan/debug pose: feet 30 cm apart and parallel, arms straight and away from body, fists clenched. Not part of the 24 manual target measurements.

rig_debug_a.label: Rig A-Pose · technical
rig_debug_a.description: Technical skinning/symmetry pose only. Never used for anthropometric measurement.

sitting_arms_lap.label: Sitting · arms on lap
sitting_arms_lap.description: Prepared for future seated length measures; not needed by the current 24-target subset.

sitting_hand_chest.label: Sitting · right hand on chest
sitting_hand_chest.description: Prepared for Abdominal Extension Depth, Sitting; outside the current 24-target subset.

poseArchitecture.rule: All displayed pose geometry derives from exactly one native SOMA/Axis16 base pose. Only numerically checkable constraints are automated before base-pose approval; complex hand/contact modifiers remain protocol instructions.
poseArchitecture.measurementOverlay: Reuses the same canonical MEAS v0.8.19.8 geometry used by sammyComputeAllMeasures(); PROT is the audit/visualization layer, not a second measurement engine.
poseArchitecture.regionPolicy: shared MEAS/PROT strict skin-weight partitions; left/right limbs never merged; no whole-body fallback for body-part measures
